_README: The SEED of a tenant's configuration: materials, vehicles, planning numbers, the fair-price model and the tenant's own settings. On first boot it is copied into the config table and from then on the Config page is the live copy; editing this file changes nothing until 'Reset to file'. A tenant package carries its own copy.
_tenant_note: name / team_label / currency / country — what a tenant calls itself and its delivery teams, the currency SYMBOL every figure is shown in (no conversion), and the ISO country that picks the country-specific providers (road restrictions, diesel index, orthophoto). Null country = none.
_materials_note: Broad, enterprise-generic categories any large-construction project recognises. Each carries a planning density (loose, as-hauled t/m3), a default input unit, whether volume<->weight conversion is meaningful, and the vehicles typically used. Densities vary with moisture/compaction; treat as editable defaults. carbon_material (10 Oct 2026) names the UK Government 2026 'Material use — Construction' class the carbon planner prices the category's material-production carbon with (aggregates, asphalt, concrete, metals, soils, average_construction); a category without one is excluded from material carbon and says so, never guessed.
_vehicles_note: Road HGVs over 3.5 t (no site plant): six UK trade-name entries, two UK truck mixers (H1, 29 Sep 2026) and three battery-electric variants of the haulage lorries — artic tipper, artic flatbed, 8-wheeler (carbon planner, 10 Oct 2026; the mixers and the smaller rigids have none yet). payload_t = typical carrying limit; emissions_kg_co2e_per_km = DESNZ 2026 GHG conversion factors, average laden, per vehicle-km, tank-to-wheel (verified 10 Oct 2026 against the gov.uk flat file v1.2; see each entry's _emissions_basis). fuel = 'diesel' (default) or 'electric'; an electric entry has no stored per-km figure — conversions._emissions() derives it as kwh_per_km × the UK electricity factor in the `carbon` block, so the two cannot drift. scenario_only: true keeps a profile out of the forecast pickers (it has no baked geometry of its own; geometry_twin names the diesel profile whose routed distances it reads). load_minutes/unload_minutes are per-vehicle turnaround estimates and override planning.load_minutes/unload_minutes, which remain the fallback. Starting estimates, not measured — edit to match your operation. 11 Oct 2026: the four EU type-approval planning entries added on 2026-09-01 were removed from the seed (and from every category list and vehicle set below); a live document or tenant package that still carries them keeps loading and resolving, because nothing in the code names them.

Artic Tipper (44t) — electric._payload_basis: ASSUMPTION, stated: the diesel twin's 29 t less 3.5 t. The ZEHID annual report 2026 (DfT / Innovate UK, zero-emission HGV and infrastructure demonstrator) reports battery-electric HGVs about 3.5 t heavier unladen, with payload down 1.5 t (42 t 4x2) to 3.5 t (6x2); the lower bound is taken. The draft UK +2 t GVW allowance for zero-emission HGVs does not lift a combination above 44 t (BVRLA; in-force status unconfirmed), so none applies at 44 t: a 44 t electric artic carries less per load. Replace with the fleet's plated figure.
Artic Tipper (44t) — electric._kwh_basis: DERIVED (mixed fleet) and an ASSUMPTION for this type: ZEHID annual report 2026 — 4,500 MWh delivered to lorries over 3.60 million km across the demonstrator fleet to 17 Jun 2026 = 1.25 kWh per km. A tipper on a short laden/empty cycle may differ; edit per profile.
Artic Tipper (44t) — electric._electric_basis: ASSUMPTION — usable battery and charger power typical of 2026 battery-electric HGVs (ZEHID-funded sites charge at 43 kW to 5 MW). Used only by the carbon planner's fleet-size comparison. Replace with the fleet's and the compound's figures.
Artic Tipper (44t) — electric._emissions_basis: DERIVED: the UK Government 2026 set has NO electric HGV factor (its HGV rows are all diesel; the EV rows are cars and vans). Carbon = kWh/km × UK electricity: generation 0.13096 (7_400_4000_5_1, Scope 2) + transmission and distribution 0.01299 (13_402_4000_5_1, Scope 3) = 0.14395 kg CO2e per kWh, 2026, verified 10 Oct 2026 against the gov.uk flat file v1.2; computed by conversions._emissions() from kwh_per_km, never stored here. Well-to-wheel adds WTT 0.03682 + 0.00359 (0.18436 in all) and is shown separately; the diesel figures on this page are tank-to-wheel. The empty/laden pair does not exist for an electric lorry; the per-leg method is NOT read by code yet.
Artic Tipper (44t) — electric._routing_note: Copied from the diesel twin: an electric lorry on the same chassis routes on the same weight and dimensions. Not baked on its own — geometry_twin is read instead.

_planning_vehicles_note: The vehicles that LEAD the Submit picker for an organisation whose country has no vehicle_sets entry (a new organisation boots with no country), in this order. Since 11 Oct 2026 they are the six UK haulage trade names, each flagged planning_vehicle: true: the array carries the ORDER and the flag marks the entry, and the two must agree (the Config page's Planning tick edits both). Left out on purpose: Rigid 4-wheeler (18t), because no material category lists it, so it would sit disabled in the lead group; Rigid 7.5t, which is not a haulage vehicle; the electric variants, which are scenario-only. The FIRST name is also the payload fallback: a forecast line whose vehicle this document does not know converts on its payload (Rigid 8-wheeler, 20 t) and says so (payload_fallback on /api/public/month-kpis and the Look-ahead). From 2026-09-01 to 11 Oct 2026 this list was four EU type-approval entries; they were removed from the product. conversions.planning_vehicle_names() never returns an empty lead list: with this array empty and no flag set it falls back to the vehicles the material categories list (see its docstring).
_planning_note: Used to estimate haul-cycle turnaround, trips/day and fleet size. load_minutes and unload_minutes here are the fallback only; a vehicle's own values take precedence.
_seasonal_note: Calendar months (1=Jan..12=Dec) with statutory HGV weight or access restrictions in the tenant's country, shown as a warning at submission when a forecast month falls in a window (and, if listed, the chosen vehicle is the restricted kind). EMPTY in the seed: a spring-thaw window is a Nordic/Baltic fact, not a product default. Add one on the Config page.
_fair_price_note: See fair_price._README. Seeded benchmarks with sources; edit on Config.

fair_price._README: 10 Sep 2026 night — the FAIR PRICE model's coefficients (backend/fairprice.py). SEEDED by the human's decision: these are public cost benchmarks, not contract rates, and each carries its source. Edit on Config -> Costing · fuel, or here and 'Reset to file'. Three are ASSUMPTIONS with no public source — vehicle_new_price_eur (behind vehicle_standing_eur_per_h), running_eur_per_km, margin_pct — replace them with the fleet's own figures. The diesel price is NOT here: it is the live EU Weekly Oil Bulletin row (fuel.py).

consumption._source: artic laden ~34 L/100 km: ICCT 'Fuel efficiency technology in European heavy-duty vehicles' (2018), regional delivery cycle; +0.4-0.95 L/100 km per tonne of payload: UK DfT 'Effects of payload on the fuel consumption of trucks' — both via lkw-control.com/en/truck-fuel-consumption-per-100-km (read 2026-09-10). The LOW end 0.4 is used, so empty = laden - 0.4 x payload, at a 26 t reference payload: artic 34 - 0.4 x 26 = 23.6. Rigid 32 t average-laden ~35 L/100 km was DERIVED (10 Sep) from the file's then DEFRA/BEIS 2025 factor 0.95 kg CO2e/km / 2.68 kg per litre, then 35 - 0.4 x 20 = 27 empty. ⚠️ H1 (29 Sep 2026): the vehicle factors above moved to the DESNZ 2026 set (rigid >17 t 0.99773 kg CO2e/km; diesel 2.58354 kg CO2e/L), on which the same derivation gives 38.6 laden and ~31 empty. The 27 is KEPT here on purpose so the seeded model's figures (test_fairprice pins them) do not move silently; replace it with the fleet's own figure, or with 31 if the derivation is preferred. The rigid figure is the weakest number in this block.

fair_price._driver_source: Statistics Estonia, Q2 2026: average gross EUR 2,243, median EUR 1,840 (stat.ee news 03.09.2026); palgad.ee lorry-driver band EUR 1,134-2,456. Taken as EUR 2,000 gross x 1.338 employer taxes (33 % social tax + 0.8 % unemployment) / 160 h / 0.85 productive = EUR 19.7/h, rounded.
fair_price._vehicle_standing_source: ASSUMPTION — no Estonian public source found. vehicle_new_price_eur 190,000 over 7 years to a 20 % residual = 21,714/yr; insurance 3 % of price = 5,700/yr; HGV road user charge EUR 1,100/yr (emta.ee, >12 t 4+ axles Euro VI); / 1,800 operating h/yr = EUR 15.8/h. Only the derivation is shown here; the price is the number to replace.
fair_price._running_source: ASSUMPTION — tyres, maintenance and repairs per km. No Estonian public source found; UK RHA cost tables put it in the EUR 0.10-0.16/km range for tippers. Replace with the fleet's own figure.
fair_price._margin_source: ASSUMPTION — a haulier's margin on top of cost. Replace with the figure the alliance considers fair.

season._source: Winter: US DOE fueleconomy.gov/feg/coldweather.shtml — cars ~15 % worse at -7 C in city driving; HGVs at road speed with warm engines suffer less, so +8 % Nov-Mar is an assumption inside a sourced range. Thaw: a FLAG on the figure, not a cost — spring axle-load limits on secondary roads in the Baltic and Nordic countries (Estonia, Transpordiamet: typically 8 t from early March to mid-April, free permits for essential transport; Virumaa Teataja, 11.03.2025). Which roads are restricted is not data the product holds. Clear thaw_months for a country without a thaw season.

fair_price._sanity_source: IRU (2025): goods transport in Europe costs EUR 0.50-2.00 per km all-in. A check on the model's output, not an input. On the test fixture (60 km round trip, 20 t, 1.73 h cycle, diesel 1.922) the model gives ~EUR 113/trip = EUR 1.88/km, and the Estonian list price found on 09 Sep (EUR 45 + 1.50/km each way) gives EUR 135 for the same trip.

_routing_note: vehicles[].routing holds HGV dimensions for HERE truck routing (weight kg, sizes cm, axle count).
_materials_vehicles_note: Which vehicles each category lists is advisory in the UI, not enforced: the Submit Forecast picker DISABLES a vehicle a category does not list (it stays visible, greyed), so every planning vehicle must be listed by at least one category or it is unselectable. The first vehicle the tenant is shown in a category's list is the Submit form's default for that material. 11 Oct 2026: the four EU type-approval entries were removed from every list. Correct any line freely.
_labels_note: labels.en per vehicle: the name the pickers show. The KEY is the canonical id and is what a forecast line stores; a label only changes what a picker shows. A missing label falls back to the key, never to an invented name. Another label language (labels.<lang>) is offered by the header's vehicle-name buttons only when a vehicle the tenant is offered carries a label in it (conversions.vehicle_labels, 'langs'). The seed's vehicles carry English only, so a new organisation is offered English alone and the header shows no buttons. Until 11 Oct 2026 the four EU type-approval entries also carried labels.eu (the EN/EU/EE toggle of 2026-09-02); a document that still carries them keeps that option for a tenant that is offered those vehicles.
_vehicle_sets_note: H1, 29 Sep 2026. Per tenant country: `lead` = the names the pickers list first (the country's trade names), `hide` = names the pickers do NOT offer to that tenant (they stay in the file and in /api/meta `vehicles`, so an existing line or baked route on one still resolves — nothing is renamed or removed, per the validator). A country not listed uses the top-level planning_vehicles as its lead list and hides nothing. Rigid 7.5t is hidden for GB: it is not a haulage vehicle on any current route. (Until 11 Oct 2026 the GB hide list also named the four EU type-approval entries, which were then removed from the seed.)
_carbon_note: Carbon planner, 10 Oct 2026 (backend/carbon.py). Material-production, disposal, electricity and tonne-km factors from the UK Government GHG conversion factors 2026 (flat file v1.2, revised 31 Jul 2026, OGL v3.0), each with its row ID, year, scope, GWP basis and a status: VERIFIED = read from the published file on 10 Oct 2026; DERIVED = arithmetic on published figures; ASSUMPTION = a planning default with no public source, to be replaced by the tenant's own figure. ICE factors are NOT used (ICE commercial use ended 30 Sep 2026). Material Use rows are AR4 GWP while transport and fuel rows are AR5 — the government publishes them so. Concrete has ONE generic figure (no grades, no GGBS): a tenant enters a supplier EPD per row instead. The NH Carbon Tool v2.7 basis is read from the tool workbook's own cells so its figure can be shown beside Wayscope's, never as the headline. The vehicle-km factors stay on each vehicle entry above.

transport._note: Wayscope's headline transport carbon is vehicle-km (trips × routed km of both legs × the vehicle's per-km factor on its entry above) — the method gov.uk says to prefer when the vehicle is known. The tonne-km rows here are the benchmark (what a tonne-km calculator would say for the same class) and the Carbon Tool basis is what the NH Carbon Tool v2.7 computes for the same tonnes and one-way distance. Shown side by side, labelled, never mixed.

rigid.row: Freighting goods › HGV (non-refrigerated, all diesel) › Rigid (>17 tonnes) › Average laden › tonne.km

artic.row: Freighting goods › HGV (non-refrigerated, all diesel) › Articulated (>33t) › Average laden › tonne.km

tonne_km_2026._implied_note: DERIVED: vehicle-km factor ÷ tonne-km factor = the national-average load the tonne-km row assumes (0.99773/0.17256; 0.93939/0.07835).

tonne_km_2026._classes_note: The benchmark row is chosen by the vehicle's size class (gvw_t): rigid ≤ 7.5 t, ≤ 17 t, > 17 t; artic ≤ 33 t, > 33 t — so a 7.5 t rigid is never measured against the > 17 t figure.

nh_carbon_tool_v27.formula: tCO2e = one_way_km × tonnes × conversion × ((laden + unladen) / 2) × 2  — sheet 'Bulk Materials' cells Y9 and Z9
nh_carbon_tool_v27.basis: UK Government conversion factors 2024 WITH well-to-tank: laden = Freighting goods › All HGVs › average laden › tonne.km 0.09752 + WTT 0.02359 kg; unladen = All HGVs › 0% laden › km 0.64392 + WTT 0.15527 kg per an assumed 7.5 t load. Read from the tool workbook 'Emissions Factors' cells G7 and G11 and the Bulk Materials / Earthworks sheet formulas on 9 Oct 2026.
nh_carbon_tool_v27.source: National Highways Carbon Tool v2.7 (September 2025) and its guidance v2.7
nh_carbon_tool_v27._note: A comparison figure only. The tool asks tonnes and one one-way distance per supplier; it has no vehicle class or payload.

nh_tool_rules._note: Mirrored from the tool's Bulk Materials and Earthworks sheets (allocation cells P–U, 'err' when the sum exceeds 100 %; the Earthworks sheet heading '(excluding bulk materials)').

vehicle_km_2026._note: The published 2026 per-vehicle-km rows (Delivery vehicles › HGV (non-refrigerated, all diesel) › average laden, Scope 1, tank-to-wheel). A vehicle whose kg CO2e/km equals one of these is shown VERIFIED with the row ID; any other typed figure is shown as an ASSUMPTION typed on Config.

benchmarks._note: No 'per delivery' limit exists in any published rule: say 'below the national average' or 'X % under baseline' (PAS 2080 baseline vs scenario).

nh_kpi_2023_prices.source: National Highways, Net Zero Highways annual progress report 2025-26, section 4 and footnote 1
nh_kpi_2023_prices._note: NH's carbon intensity of maintenance and construction, tCO2e per £m spent, restated at 2023 price levels (OBR March 2026 CPI). It rose from 159 to 181. It supersedes the 210 → 148 (2023/24 → 2024/25) of the Net Zero Highways plan 2025 update, which this block carried until 11 Oct 2026. Context only: NH's figure covers all its maintenance and construction, a different scope from the Carbon page.
